# ChessPulse

ChessPulse is a local desktop app for reviewing a chess.com session after you play. It keeps a pulse trace beside the clock and the moves, then asks whether a bad stretch was a state problem or a chess problem.

It is not a chess trainer, not an engine overlay, and not a medical device. It makes no diagnosis.

The app does not watch a rated game. There is no engine, evaluation, or advice while a game is live. You play on chess.com. ChessPulse looks at the session afterwards.

## Run

Requirements: Node 22, npm, and a display.

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env
npm test
npm run dev
```

`npm test` is the unit suite. `npm run test:consent` is separate: it builds `dist/` and `dist-electron/` first, then opens Electron. It is not part of `npm test` and does not run without that build.

`npm run dev` opens the window against the local page at `http://127.0.0.1:5173`. `npm run build` then `npm start` opens the built page from disk.

If Electron aborts because the sandbox helper is not setuid, start the built app with `--no-sandbox`. That flag is a development workaround.

```bash
npx electron --no-sandbox .
```

The SmartSpectra key and any model key belong in `.env` only. `.env.example` lists the names and stays empty. The current window does not call the camera SDK or a model.

## Consent and data

The camera stays off until you press **Allow the camera**. Revoking consent stops an open session. Video is granted only to the main frame of this app's own built page, not to every file on disk, and only for the camera, not the microphone or the screen. The dev page is `http://127.0.0.1:5173`, so it can record consent and still cannot open the camera.

A session is a folder of numbers: `meta.json` and `samples.ndjson`. No image or video file is written. The folder is under `$XDG_DATA_HOME/chesspulse` or `~/.local/share/chesspulse`. Deleting that folder deletes the session. Nothing in the app is uploaded, and there is no account.

## Current limits

The sensing screen draws pulse samples the main process has stored. It breaks the line when samples are more than one second apart. The SDK is not connected yet, so starting a session does not produce a live trace. Pasting games, the engine, and the report are not in this build.

## S12 — PGN parser

Commit `bd82b6a`.

A pasted game is text. `parsePgn` reads the headers and the move list. `parsePgnBatch` does that for up to 20 games, then either returns the games or a refusal. `thinkTimeSec` is separate: it does not change the stored game.

Clock comment `[%clk H:MM:SS.d]` becomes `clockSec` on that move. Think time for a move is the previous remaining clock for that side, minus the new clock, plus the increment from `TimeControl`. The first move of each side starts from the base time (`180+2` is 180 seconds plus 2; `60` is 60 seconds and no increment). If a clock is missing, that side's think time stays `null` from then on. It is not stored as zero.

`EndDate` plus `EndTime`, and `UTCDate` plus `UTCTime`, become epoch milliseconds. The three real chess.com exports used for the earlier proof have clocks and none of those timestamps.

Order uses end times when every game has one. If none do, and every game has a UTC start, it uses those starts. If no game has either, the batch is accepted and marked `unverified`. If only some games have a time, the batch is rejected and the missing indexes are named. Aborted and abandoned games stay in the summary and have `includeInStats: false`.

Checked by `src/main/analysis/pgn.test.ts`. The real proof games were parsed locally (38, 63, and 58 clocked moves) and were not copied into the repository.

Limitation: the parser accepts SAN-shaped text. `positionsFromMoves` replays it. An illegal move stops the line and does not invent the next board. `chess.js` 1.4 omits the en-passant square when no capture is legal, so the FEN after `1. e4` ends in `-`, not `e3`.

## S13 — engine worker

Commit `0984eed`.

`positionsFromMoves` turns SAN into the FEN before and after each move. `createEngine` keeps one Stockfish 19.0.1 `lite-single` worker. Each search sends `ucinewgame` first. Without that, a second search of the starting position reused the hash and returned a different centipawn score (26, then 32). The score kept is the exact requested depth, and bound lines are ignored. A mate is stored as `mate`, not converted into a fake centipawn value.

A bad FEN, a search that does not answer within 5 seconds, an engine error, or a batch older than 20 minutes comes back as `evalFailed` with a reason. No score is filled in. The worker does not see pulse samples.

Checked by `src/main/engine.test.ts` and `src/main/analysis/positions.test.ts`. Sixty depth-8 searches finished inside the 150 ms average bound. The same starting position produced the same score twice.

Limitation: this does not yet turn those scores into centipawn loss. That computation is S14. D-03, the GPL licence question for distributing Stockfish, is still open.

## S14 — centipawn loss, bands, accuracy, verdict

Commit `7ce7bd8`.

A move's centipawn loss is the side-to-move score before the move plus the side-to-move score after it, and never below zero. The engine reports each score from the side about to move, so a preserved advantage comes back as the opposite sign and the loss is zero. A mate, or a failed search, has no loss and is not called a blunder.

Win chance uses the published Lichess curve, `100 / (1 + e^(-0.00368208 * cp))`, from <https://lichess.org/page/accuracy>. Move accuracy uses that site's formula, including the +1 analysis bonus, clamped to 0–100. A blunder is a drop of at least 30 win-percent points. Accuracy for a band is the mean of those move accuracies, rounded. Fewer than five scored moves is `insufficient` and the object has no accuracy number. Aborted and abandoned moves are left out when `includeInStats` is false.

Elevated means at or above the session baseline plus 10 bpm. The same pulses change band when the baseline changes.

The verdict is one sentence built only from those numbers. The between-games clause is appended only when the caller supplies it. This module does not call a model.

Checked by `src/main/analysis/metrics.test.ts`. Calling the summary twice returns the same object. Building the whole report twice, and diffing that JSON, waits for the report builder.

## S15 — alignment

Commit `554ffc4`.

Wall time and the monotonic sample clock meet in one conversion. With only the start anchor, microseconds and epoch milliseconds scale by 1 000. When the stop anchor is present, the conversion is a straight line between the two anchors, so a drift between the clocks is not ignored.

A game with `EndTime` ends at that converted time. Its start is the end minus the sum of think times. The mode is `endtime` and the tolerance is 1 second, the bound already measured for the anchor. There is no banner.

A game with a UTC start and no `EndTime` starts at that converted time. The mode is `starttime`. The banner is the blueprint sentence, and the tolerance is ±90 seconds.

A game with neither timestamp, which is the real chess.com export, is packed in paste order from the session start. The mode is `inferred`. The tolerance is the unused time left in the session. The banner names both missing fields and that bound. No between-game wait is reported, because those waits were not observed. Without a session stop, or without move clocks, nothing is placed.

A pulse hole inside a placed game is the time a usable sample does not cover. A weak sample does not close it. A measured wait between two timestamped games is a gap. The four-minute case is 240 seconds.

Checked by `src/main/analysis/align.test.ts`. A live game on a real captured trace is still NOT_RUN.

## S16 — report builder

Commit `5084544`.

`buildReport` reads a stored session and pasted PGN text. It recomputes coverage from the samples. Under 70% it returns `Refusal{reason:'low_coverage'}` with the measured percent, the threshold, and the lighting remedy, and it deletes any previous `report.json`. It does not run the engine and it does not include a verdict or bands.

At or above 70% it parses, aligns, scores each move, and writes `report.json`. The command prints one line, the verdict. The same session and PGNs built twice return the same object. The test PGNs are written by the test. The builder does not load `tests/fixtures/`.

The printed line from the covered test session was: `0 blunders, 0 of them while your pulse was elevated. Accuracy settled insufficient, elevated insufficient.` One move is not enough for a band percentage, so both bands stay unnumbered.

A later review tightened the same path. An excluded game with no clocks no longer blocks placement of a finished game. A negative clock delta is rejected. Packed games that run past the session stop are not placed, and leftover time is rounded up to the next second. The parser rejects setup positions, impossible dates, a movetext result that disagrees with the `Result` tag, and joined moves such as `e4e5`. A mate or a failed search is left out of the blunder count and the verdict says so.

Run it with `npm run report -- --root <data-dir> <sessionId> <game.pgn>`.

# Node.js and Electron SDK (https://smartspectra.presagetech.com/docs/nodejs)

> For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://smartspectra.presagetech.com/llms.txt). Any documentation page is available as markdown by appending `.md` to its URL.

# @smartspectra/node-sdk

Pure-FFI Node.js (Electron) binding for SmartSpectra vitals measurement.
[koffi](https://koffi.dev) loads the SmartSpectra C ABI shim at runtime —
no native addon, no `binding.gyp`, no `electron-rebuild`, no `node-gyp`.

## Start here

- Electron sample: [electron-quickstart](https://github.com/Presage-Security/SmartSpectra/tree/main/nodejs/samples/electron-quickstart)
- API reference: <https://smartspectra.presagetech.com/docs/nodejs/api-reference>
- Device Readiness: [check readiness and handle results](https://smartspectra.presagetech.com/docs/nodejs/device-readiness.md)
- Metrics guide: <https://smartspectra.presagetech.com/docs/nodejs/metrics>

## Architecture

```text
┌──────────────────────────┐
│ your Node / Electron app │
└───────────┬──────────────┘
            │ require('@smartspectra/node-sdk')
┌───────────▼──────────────┐
│ js/index.js              │  public surface
│ js/smartspectra.js       │  SmartSpectraSDK class
│ js/ffi.js                │  koffi types + Session
│ js/resolve-native.js     │  shim path resolver
└───────────┬──────────────┘
            │ koffi.load()
┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ @smartspectra/node-sdk-<plat>-<arch>/  │  self-contained native runtime,
│   libsmartspectra_capi.*               │  shipped as a dependency package;
│   …bundled runtime libraries…          │  load paths pre-relocated to
│                                        │  @loader_path / $ORIGIN /
└────────────────────────────────────────┘  adjacent-DLL search
```

The native runtime ships in per-platform packages
(`@smartspectra/node-sdk-<plat>-<arch>`) pulled in as dependencies of the main
package. There is **no install script** in the published tarball and no
postinstall download; the binding loads the package matching your machine at
runtime. SDK-thread callbacks are marshalled onto the V8 event loop by koffi
thread-safe trampolines.

## Supported Platforms

| Platform | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS Apple Silicon (`darwin-arm64`) | Supported | Electron and headless Node workflows supported |
| Linux x64 (`linux-x64`) | Supported | Requires glibc 2.35+ |
| Linux ARM64 (`linux-arm64`) | Supported | Requires glibc 2.35+ |
| Windows x64 (`win32-x64`) | Supported | Electron and headless Node workflows supported |

## Common Prerequisites

| Requirement | Version |
| --- | --- |
| Node.js | >= 20 (Node 24 LTS recommended) |
| Electron (optional) | >= 28 |

You also need an API key from
[physiology.presagetech.com](https://physiology.presagetech.com/auth/login). An AI assistant
connected to the [SmartSpectra MCP Server](https://smartspectra.presagetech.com/docs/mcp-server.md) can fetch it from your account
for you.

The native runtime ships in per-platform npm packages pulled in automatically
as dependencies — no install script and no system libraries to install.

Supported platforms: `darwin-arm64`, `linux-x64`, `linux-arm64`, `win32-x64`.

On Linux the native runtime is built on Ubuntu 22.04 (Jammy), so it requires
glibc >= 2.35 — Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+, or any distribution at least that
new. glibc and libstdc++ are provided by your system, not bundled.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @smartspectra/node-sdk
```

Early adopters can track the latest release candidate with the `rc` dist-tag:

```bash
npm install @smartspectra/node-sdk@rc
```

The native packages (`@smartspectra/node-sdk-<platform>-<arch>`) come in as
dependencies and the binding loads the one matching your `platform`/`arch` at
runtime. Each is self-contained — it bundles everything the binding loads at
runtime, with paths already rewritten at publish time, so nothing needs to be on
PATH and no system libraries are required. There is no install script.

> **Note** — `npm install` downloads the native runtime for every supported
> platform (a few hundred MB total), not just your host's. This is expected;
> only the package matching your machine is loaded at runtime.

If your platform is unsupported (no `@smartspectra/node-sdk-<plat>-<arch>` is
published for it), the first `require()` fails with an actionable error naming
the missing package.

## Pick Your Integration Path

- Electron desktop app: use `@smartspectra/node-sdk/main`,
  `@smartspectra/node-sdk/preload`, and `@smartspectra/node-sdk/renderer`.
- Headless Node process with a local camera: use `@smartspectra/node-sdk`
  directly with `useCamera(CameraSelection.default)`.
- Headless or server-side Node process with host-provided frames: use
  `useCustomInput()` / `sendFrame()`.
- Runnable reference app: [electron-quickstart](https://github.com/Presage-Security/SmartSpectra/tree/main/nodejs/samples/electron-quickstart)

## Camera Quickstart

> The snippets below are ES modules (`import` + top-level `await`) — save them as `.mjs`, or
> set `"type": "module"` in your `package.json`. In a CommonJS project, use `require()` and
> wrap the `await` calls in an `async` function.

```ts
import { SmartSpectraSDK, CameraSelection, breathingMetrics, cardioMetrics, decodeMetrics } from '@smartspectra/node-sdk';

const sdk = new SmartSpectraSDK({
  apiKey: 'YOUR_API_KEY',
  requestedMetrics: [...breathingMetrics, ...cardioMetrics],
});

sdk.on('processingStatus', (status) => console.log('Processing status:', status));
sdk.on('validationStatus', (code, ts, hint) =>
  console.log('Validation:', code, hint, 'at', ts, 'µs'));
sdk.on('metrics', (buf, ts) => {
  console.log('Metrics at', ts, 'µs:', decodeMetrics(buf));
});
sdk.on('error', (code, message, retryable) =>
  console.error('SmartSpectra error', code, message, 'retryable=', retryable));

sdk.useCamera(CameraSelection.default);
sdk.start();

console.log('Measuring from the default camera. Press Ctrl+C to stop.');

// On shutdown:
process.on('SIGINT', async () => {
  await sdk.stopAsync();
  await sdk.destroy();
  process.exit(0);
});
```

`useCamera(CameraSelection.default)` selects the default camera while stopped; capture begins at
`start()`. You can discover cameras without creating an SDK instance:

```ts
import { CameraSelection, SmartSpectraSDK } from '@smartspectra/node-sdk';

const cameras = SmartSpectraSDK.availableCameras();
if (cameras.length > 0) {
  sdk.useCamera(CameraSelection.byId(cameras[0].id), { width: 1280, height: 720 });
}
```

Windows, `.front` and `.back` fail with `kInputUnavailable` because facing is
not reported. See the
[migration guide](https://smartspectra.presagetech.com/docs/nodejs/migration-guide.md) and [API reference](https://smartspectra.presagetech.com/docs/nodejs/api-reference.md#cameraoptions).

### 3.2 The system in one paragraph

One Electron app. The **main process** owns everything native: it opens the camera through the
SmartSpectra Node SDK, receives confidence-tagged pulse samples, writes them to a local append-only
store, and exposes them to the UI over IPC. The **renderer** is a single-column instrument: start,
sensing, between-games, paste, report, reading. After the session ends, the renderer sends pasted
PGNs to main, which parses each game (moves, `[%clk]`, `EndTime`, result), runs a local WASM
engine over the positions, converts evaluation swings into centipawn loss, and computes bands from
the stored pulse trace. A pure analysis module then aligns games to the trace on a shared time axis,
applies the coverage gate, aggregates accuracy per band, and produces the numbers that the verdict
line and the charts render. Everything computed is local; nothing leaves the machine except, if the
user supplies a key, PGN plus summary statistics to an AI provider for narrative text.

### 3.3 Main data flow

```text
camera ──► SDK (main) ──► samples[] {t, bpm, confidence} ──► local store (session id)
                                                                    │
PGN paste ──► parse (moves, clk, EndTime, result) ──► engine pass ──┤
                                                                    ▼
                                          analysis: align ─► gate ─► band ─► aggregate
                                                                    │
                                            ┌───────────────────────┼──────────────────┐
                                            ▼                       ▼                  ▼
                                     timeline series        verdict line        coach threshold
                                            │                                          │
                                            └────────► renderer (charts, copy) ◄───────┘
                                                                    │
                                       optional: PGN + summary stats ──► AI provider ──► INFERRED panels
```

### 3.4 Important tradeoffs

| Tradeoff | Choice and reason |
|---|---|
| Live responsiveness vs. stability | The 12 s averaging window is what makes the trace meaningful; the coach line therefore reacts in tens of seconds, not instantly. Stated in the UI rather than hidden. |
| Drop low-confidence samples vs. keep them | Drop from aggregation, keep on the raw trace, and let coverage fall. Deleting them would inflate apparent quality. |
| `EndTime` vs. file mtime | `EndTime` when present; explicit low-confidence mode otherwise. Never silently substitute a guess. |
| WASM engine vs. native binary | WASM removes architecture and bundling failures at a real speed cost; the shallow pass is scoped to absorb that cost. |
| One long session vs. many short ones | One session keeps alignment cheap and the demo honest, at the price of a smaller sample. |
| SQLite vs. JSON files | Decided in §6; whatever wins must survive restarts and be inspectable without the app. |

### 3.5 What I should be able to explain before Prompt 2 starts

1. Why the SDK cannot run in the renderer, and what crosses IPC because of it.
2. What a confidence value does to a sample, and what coverage means arithmetically.

# Phase 1 — foundation

Branch `foundation`, plus the SDK ingestion that completed S11 on `main` (2026-11-21).

## How to run

From the repository root:

```text
npm install
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run dev
```

The main process reads `.env` at startup. Sensing needs `SMARTSPECTRA_API_KEY`; a value already
exported by the shell wins over the file.

## S8–S11 — shell, store, session, strip

Already recorded in the code and the decisions log. Brief shape:

- `src/main/index.ts` opens one sandboxed window, installs the CSP, and registers six IPC handles.
- `src/main/store.ts` writes `meta.json` atomically and appends `samples.ndjson` under a
  per-session lock.
- `src/main/session.ts` owns start/stop, the median baseline, coverage, and crash recovery.
- `src/renderer/SensingStrip.tsx` draws the stored samples and breaks the line on a gap.

## S11b — SmartSpectra capture bridge

Added 2026-11-21. This closes the gap left at Phase 1 exit: the sample sink existed but nothing
in the product fed it, so a session could only contain samples written by tests.

### What was done and why

- `src/main/env.ts` loads `.env` into `process.env` once, before the window opens. Electron and
  Node do not read `.env` on their own, so `cp .env.example .env` previously did nothing.
  Existing non-empty environment values are kept. Values are never logged; only the number of
  loaded keys is.
- `src/main/capture.ts` owns one `SmartSpectraSDK` per session. It requests the cardio bundle
  (`PULSE_RATE`, `ARTERIAL_PRESSURE_TRACE`, `HRV`), disables telemetry, and opens the default
  camera with `useCamera(CameraSelection.default)`.
- `src/main/capture-samples.ts` is the pure boundary: decoded protobuf → `PulseSample`, SDK error
  codes → player-readable copy, validation codes → a hint. Keeping it free of the native binding
  is what makes it testable in plain Node.
- `src/main/index.ts` starts capture only after the session header exists and stops capture
  before closing the session, so the final batch has a session to land in. Validation and SDK
  errors travel on `cp:validation` and `cp:sdk:error`, as the blueprint's IPC table names them.
- `src/preload/index.ts` and `src/renderer/App.tsx` show the SDK's own hint while sensing, and a
  terminal SDK error moves the screen to "Sensing stopped" with the specific reason.
- `src/main/consent.ts` gained an `onRevoked` hook. The renderer already stops the session before
  it revokes; the hook is the process-level guarantee that the camera is released even if the
  page never gets that far.

### Data and control flow

```text
camera ─► SmartSpectraSDK (main) ─► decodeMetrics ─► latestPulseSample
                                                         │  (epoch µs → session mono µs)
                                                         ▼
                                            250 ms batch ─► ingestSamples ─► samples.ndjson
                                                                  │
                                                                  └─► cp:sample:batch ─► strip
```

Validation and errors take a parallel path: SDK event → `capture-samples` copy → IPC → the one
status line under the heading.

### Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — PASS (electron + renderer configs).
- `npm test` — PASS, 134/134. New: `env.test.ts` (file parsing and precedence) and
  `capture-samples.test.ts` (clock conversion, Long timestamps, impossible values, monotonic
  rejection, error copy).
- `npm run build` — PASS; the renderer bundle is unchanged in behaviour.
- `node -e "require('@smartspectra/node-sdk').SmartSpectraSDK.version"` → `3.5.0`, native runtime
  loads on this machine (glibc 2.43, linux-x64).
- `npx electron --no-sandbox .` — PASS; window opens and logs
  `[chesspulse] loaded 5 setting(s) from .env`.
- Real SDK failure path, with a deliberately invalid key: `start()` returns, the `error` event
  arrives with code `2`, the mapped copy is *"The SmartSpectra key was rejected. Check
  SMARTSPECTRA_API_KEY in .env."*, `retryable=false`, and `stop()` resolves after
  `stopAsync`/`destroy`. No camera measurement was taken.
- A real captured session with the user's key — **NOT_RUN**. That is the P1 proof and needs the
  player seated in front of the camera; it is not an agent-initiated experiment.

### Limitations and risks

- The main-process camera path bypasses Chromium's permission handler. Consent is enforced in
  `index.ts` before `startCapture`; the renderer permission handler remains as defence, not as
  the guarantee.
- No live camera preview is shown. The strip and the "Sensing" line are the indicators; the OS
  camera LED is the third.
- Only the newest pulse in each payload is stored. If the SDK ever batched several new samples
  per event, older ones in that payload would be skipped. The trace stays sparse rather than
  wrong; coverage would fall honestly.
- A retryable error leaves the pipeline reported but not restarted. The player can stop and start
  again. There is no automatic re-auth loop, deliberately: retries cost network and can bill.
- The 8 s stop timeout means a wedged native pipeline cannot block the window forever, but the
  camera handle is then only released by `destroy()`.
- `D-03` (Stockfish GPL distribution) remains open and is unrelated to this step.

## Checkpoint to read

- **Measured vs computed:** the SDK measures pulse; the main process only converts its clock and
  drops impossible values. Baseline, coverage, bands and the verdict remain computed elsewhere.
- **Why capture lives in the main process:** the key must never enter the page, the page has no
  Node, and the renderer-owned MediaStream path would put the camera in the sandboxed document.
  The page therefore sees numbers, not frames.
- **Why weak samples are stored:** coverage is the honesty mechanism. Deleting a weak sample
  would raise apparent quality; keeping it lowers coverage, and the gate refuses.

placing them in the same directory as `<your-app>.exe` is the simplest

they resolve siblings without any `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` plumbing.

host system — they are not vendored in the platform package.

## Logging

SDK log verbosity defaults to warnings and errors only. To change it, pass
`logLevel` in the SDK options:

```js
const { SmartSpectraSDK, SmartSpectraLogLevel } = require('@smartspectra/node-sdk');

const sdk = new SmartSpectraSDK({
    apiKey: '...',
    logLevel: SmartSpectraLogLevel.kInfo,
});
```

Levels are cumulative — `kDebug`, `kInfo`, `kWarning` (default), `kError`,
`kNone`. `kDebug` cannot restore debug-only statements compiled out of the
release engine binary.

## Performance notes

- koffi adds ~100 ns per FFI call — negligible for `sendFrame()` at 30 fps.
- SDK callbacks arrive on worker threads; koffi marshals them onto the V8
  event loop, so listeners run on the main thread.
- In Electron, the renderer-side SDK (`@smartspectra/node-sdk/renderer`)
  captures frames in the renderer and ships them to the main process —
  simplest to wire and fine for typical use. For the lowest latency at high
  resolution, capture in the main process instead (`desktopCapturer` or an
  off-screen renderer), since renderer→main IPC adds frame-time latency that
  scales with resolution.

| `kAuthenticationFailed` | API key issue | Check the key + the keychain entitlement on macOS |
| `kNonMonotonicTimestamp` | Wall-clock timestamps | Use `process.hrtime.bigint() / 1000n` (monotonic) |

### What was done and why

- `src/main/env.ts` loads `.env` into `process.env` once, before the window opens. Electron and
  Node do not read `.env` on their own, so `cp .env.example .env` previously did nothing.
  Existing non-empty environment values are kept. Values are never logged; only the number of
  loaded keys is.
- `src/main/capture.ts` owns one `SmartSpectraSDK` per session. It requests only
  `MetricType.PULSE_RATE` — the one metric the app displays — rather than the whole cardio
  bundle, so no unread output is requested. (The SDK's model graph still fetches
  `phasic-bp-inference` during start; the probe log below shows it even with pulse alone.)
  Telemetry is disabled, and the camera is opened with `useCamera(CameraSelection.default)`.
- `src/main/capture-samples.ts` is the pure boundary: decoded protobuf → `PulseSample`, SDK error
  codes → player-readable copy, validation codes → a hint. Keeping it free of the native binding
  is what makes it testable in plain Node.
- `src/main/index.ts` starts capture only after the session header exists and stops capture
  before closing the session, so the final batch has a session to land in. Validation and SDK
  errors travel on `cp:validation` and `cp:sdk:error`, as the blueprint's IPC table names them.
- `src/preload/index.ts` and `src/renderer/App.tsx` show the SDK's own hint while sensing, and a
  terminal SDK error moves the screen to "Sensing stopped" with the specific reason.
- `src/main/consent.ts` gained an `onRevoked` hook. The renderer already stops the session before
  it revokes; the hook is the process-level guarantee that the camera is released even if the
  page never gets that far.

### Data and control flow

```text
camera ─► SmartSpectraSDK (main) ─► decodeMetrics ─► latestPulseSample
                                                         │  (epoch µs → session mono µs)
                                                         ▼
                                            250 ms batch ─► ingestSamples ─► samples.ndjson
                                                                  │
                                                                  └─► cp:sample:batch ─► strip
```

Validation and errors take a parallel path: SDK event → `capture-samples` copy → IPC → the one
status line under the heading.

### Frame rate

The on-device pipeline needs a sustained camera frame rate — don't let the camera fall below
roughly **25 fps**; target 30 fps for headroom. This is usually automatic on modern devices, but
two things can undermine it:

- Low light, which can cause the camera's auto-exposure to lengthen exposure time and drop frame
  rate to compensate — another reason to fix lighting first if you see intermittent frame-rate
  warnings.
- Heavy on-device CPU/GPU contention from other work happening at the same time as capture.

## Confidence and warm-up time

Every rate-based metric ships with a `confidence` value (0–100) and a `stable` flag alongside the
value itself — treat both as part of the reading, not just the number:

- **Confidence starts at 0** and only becomes meaningful once the metric's analysis window has
  filled: 30 seconds for breathing rate and the breathing waveforms, 60 seconds for HRV, 12
  seconds for pulse rate. Don't surface or act on a reading before its window has elapsed —
  early "0 confidence" samples are expected, not a bug.
- **`stable`** indicates whether the underlying detection (face, landmarks, etc.) is currently
  reliable frame-to-frame. Treat `stable: false` the same way you'd treat a validation warning:
  something in the capture (framing, motion, lighting) is currently degraded.

See [Data Types](https://smartspectra.presagetech.com/docs/data-types.md) for the full payload schema.

## Reading the SDK's live feedback

The SDK continuously evaluates the incoming frames and reports a `ValidationStatus` — a stable
`code` plus a human-readable `hint` string — so you don't have to guess why a measurement looks
bad. Surface the `hint` text directly to end users; it's designed to be shown as-is.

| Code | Meaning | What to tell the user |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OK` | Frame passes all checks. | Nothing — this is the "good" state. |
| `NO_FACE_FOUND` | No face detected in frame. | Get a face into frame, facing the camera. |
| `MULTIPLE_FACES_FOUND` | More than one face detected. | Make sure only one person is in frame. |
| `FACE_NOT_CENTERED` | Face detected but off-center horizontally (left/right). | Center your face in the frame. |
| `TOO_DARK` | Image is underexposed. | Add light, or move to a brighter area. |
| `TOO_BRIGHT` | Image is overexposed. | Reduce light, or move away from a bright/backlit source. |
| `CHEST_NOT_VISIBLE` | Chest not visible or too far away (breathing/chest metrics). | Reframe so the upper chest is visible. |
| `CAMERA_TUNING` | Camera is still auto-adjusting exposure/focus. | Wait a moment before recording. |
| `FRAME_RATE_TOO_LOW` | Sustained camera frame rate has dropped too low. | Improve lighting (see above) or reduce concurrent device load. |
| `EXCESSIVE_MOTION` | Body or head motion exceeds the reliable-measurement threshold. | Hold still — motion may affect accuracy. |

I measured four input paths against the real SDK on this machine:

| Input path | Frames accepted | metrics events | pulse readings |
|---|---|---|---|
| Page camera → `sendFrame`, 16:9 | yes | **0** | 0 |

1. The **main process owns the camera** (`useCamera(default)`), which is the path that measures.
2. The preview is a **tap on the SDK's own output** (`videoOutput` → 320 px RGBA, ~12 fps → `cp:preview`). The page never opens a camera, so it can't fight the SDK for the device and can't be starved by window throttling.
